status: Source-derived operational interpretations; human review pending; not facility-approved SOPs

rules.scenario: patients ask which services are available
rules.guidance: Use the facility's published service information to explain availability and any stated charges; do not invent prices.

citation.anchor: the types, availability and cost

rules.scenario: patients ask how services are organized
rules.guidance: Use the published organization of services to direct patients to the appropriate administrative service point.

citation.anchor: the organization of health services

rules.scenario: a patient asks when to attend
rules.guidance: Check the facility's published operating schedule and visiting timetable before communicating attendance information.

citation.anchor: operating schedules and timetables of visits

rules.scenario: a patient asks how to access a clinic
rules.guidance: Explain the facility's published access procedure rather than inventing a booking route or promising an unavailable slot.

citation.anchor: procedures for access to the health services

rules.scenario: patients ask about their responsibilities at a visit
rules.guidance: Direct patients to the applicable service charter and published rights and duties for the facility.

citation.anchor: the rights and duties of users and healthcare providers

rules.scenario: a waiting-area interaction becomes disrespectful
rules.guidance: Handle the interaction respectfully and protect the patient's privacy while arranging administrative assistance.

citation.anchor: treated with dignity, respect and have their privacy respected

rules.scenario: a patient cannot understand information about a planned visit
rules.guidance: Arrange for the healthcare provider to explain the information in an understandable language and manner appropriate to the patient's literacy.

citation.anchor: in a language that the user understands

rules.scenario: patients ask reception to explain treatment options before booking
rules.guidance: Connect the patient with the healthcare provider for the benefits, risks, costs and consequences of the options; reception must not make clinical recommendations.

citation.anchor: benefits, risks, costs and consequences

rules.scenario: a patient asks which facility rules apply during attendance
rules.guidance: Point the patient to the facility's published rules for using its services and clarify administrative requirements without inventing restrictions.

citation.anchor: adhere to the rules of a health facility

rules.scenario: a scheduling consent notice does not identify the organization
rules.guidance: Have the responsible data team identify the controller or processor in the notice before seeking consent for the scheduling-data use.

citation.anchor: the identity of the data controller or data processor

rules.scenario: one consent form covers several appointment-data uses
rules.guidance: Explain each processing purpose separately when consent is the basis for using appointment information.

citation.anchor: the purpose of each of the processing operations

rules.scenario: a patient asks what appointment data consent covers
rules.guidance: Explain the types of personal data collected and used for the consent-based appointment process.

citation.anchor: the type of personal data that is collected and used

rules.scenario: a scheduling consent notice omits third-party sharing
rules.guidance: Include whether personal data will be shared with third parties before seeking consent for that processing.

citation.anchor: whether the personal data processed shall be shared with third parties

rules.scenario: a patient asks whether appointment-data consent can be withdrawn
rules.guidance: Explain the right to withdraw consent and route a withdrawal request to the team responsible for the relevant processing.

citation.anchor: the right to withdraw consent

rules.scenario: a patient is uncertain about giving optional scheduling-data consent
rules.guidance: Explain the implications of giving, withholding or withdrawing that consent without pressuring the patient.

citation.anchor: the implications of providing, withholding or withdrawing consent

rules.scenario: the team is choosing how to communicate a consent notice
rules.guidance: Use an accessible notice format; the regulations allow written, oral, audio or video communication of consent information.

citation.anchor: written notice, oral statement, audio or video message

rules.scenario: a scheduler is unsure whether a person can give data-processing consent
rules.guidance: Refer the capacity question to the responsible team before relying on consent; do not make a clinical capacity assessment at reception.

citation.anchor: data subject has capacity to give consent

rules.scenario: patients feel pressured to agree to optional appointment-data use
rules.guidance: Ensure consent is voluntary; refer pressure or coercion concerns to the responsible privacy team.

citation.anchor: data subject voluntarily gives consent

rules.scenario: a scheduler wants to reuse general consent for a new task
rules.guidance: Confirm that consent specifically covers the proposed processing purpose before relying on it.

citation.anchor: consent is specific to the purpose of processing

rules.scenario: a scheduler treats silence as agreement to optional messaging
rules.guidance: Do not presume consent merely because the patient did not object to the proposed processing.

citation.anchor: it is presumed on the basis that the data subject did not object

rules.scenario: a form makes optional data consent non-negotiable
rules.guidance: Refer the form for correction; presenting consent as non-negotiable undermines freely given consent.

citation.anchor: it is presented as a non-negotiable part

rules.scenario: a patient fears a penalty for refusing optional data use
rules.guidance: Escalate the consent design for review when refusal or withdrawal would cause detriment.

citation.anchor: the data subject is unable to refuse or withdraw their consent without detriment

rules.scenario: scheduling and promotional purposes are bundled together
rules.guidance: Separate the processing purposes and seek specific consent for each purpose when relying on consent.

citation.anchor: merges several purposes for processing without seeking

rules.scenario: a patient's reply about optional messages is unclear
rules.guidance: Clarify the patient's intention before treating an ambiguous reply as consent.

citation.anchor: the intention of the data subject is ambiguous

rules.scenario: a patient withdraws consent to one optional appointment-data use
rules.guidance: Route the withdrawal for restriction of the affected processing, subject to the applicable statutory exceptions; do not assume all healthcare records must be deleted.

citation.anchor: restrict the part of the processing in respect of which consent is withdrawn

rules.scenario: a registration process exposes personal details unnecessarily
rules.guidance: Arrange registration in a way that respects the patient's privacy and refer the exposure for correction.

citation.anchor: processed in accordance with the right to privacy

rules.scenario: a registration practice is unclear to patients
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team ensure that the processing is lawful, fair and transparent to patients.

citation.anchor: processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner

rules.scenario: a new registration field has no defined purpose
rules.guidance: Ask the data owner to define a specific legitimate purpose before collecting the additional information.

citation.anchor: collected for explicit, specified and legitimate purposes

rules.scenario: a registration form requests excessive information
rules.guidance: Limit collection to information necessary and relevant to the stated registration purpose.

citation.anchor: adequate, relevant, limited to what is necessary

rules.scenario: a form asks about private family affairs
rules.guidance: Provide a valid explanation for requiring family or private information and refer unnecessary questions for removal.

citation.anchor: valid explanation is provided whenever information relating to family

rules.scenario: a patient reports outdated registration details
rules.guidance: Route the correction promptly so the responsible records team keeps personal information accurate and up to date.

citation.anchor: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date

rules.scenario: the team proposes keeping identifiable registration data forever
rules.guidance: Apply the approved purpose-based retention process rather than indefinite retention by default.

citation.anchor: no longer than is necessary for the purposes

rules.scenario: a patient asks why registration information is used
rules.guidance: Explain the intended uses of the patient's personal data or connect them with the responsible data team.

citation.anchor: to be informed of the use to which their personal data

rules.scenario: a patient wants access to their registration record
rules.guidance: Route the request through the facility's data-access process rather than dismissing the patient's access right.

citation.anchor: to access their personal data in custody

rules.scenario: a patient objects to a registration-data use
rules.guidance: Record and route the objection to the responsible data team for assessment under the applicable process.

citation.anchor: to object to the processing of all or part

rules.scenario: a patient identifies misleading information in their record
rules.guidance: Help the patient submit a correction request to the responsible records team.

citation.anchor: to correction of false or misleading data

rules.scenario: a patient asks to delete false information
rules.guidance: Route the deletion request to the responsible data team; do not promise unrestricted deletion of the entire health record.

citation.anchor: to deletion of false or misleading data about them

rules.scenario: a guardian seeks to exercise a child's data rights
rules.guidance: Use the representative-rights process to establish parental authority or guardianship before handling the child's request.

citation.anchor: where the data subject is a minor

rules.scenario: a representative requests records for a person with a disability
rules.guidance: Establish the representative's authority as guardian or administrator through the responsible team; do not assume disability alone removes the person's rights.

citation.anchor: person duly authorised to act as their guardian or administrator

rules.scenario: a patient appoints someone to make a data-rights request
rules.guidance: Verify the representative's authorization through the facility's process before handling the request on the patient's behalf.

citation.anchor: person duly authorised by the data subject

rules.scenario: a registrar chooses where to obtain patient information
rules.guidance: Collect information directly from the patient as the default; refer proposed exceptions for assessment rather than assuming indirect collection is always permitted.

citation.anchor: collect personal data directly from the data subject

rules.scenario: a registrar proposes obtaining information from another source with consent
rules.guidance: Confirm the patient's consent covers collection from that source and use the approved collection process.

citation.anchor: consented to the collection from another source

rules.scenario: a registration notice omits patient data rights
rules.guidance: Include information about the patient's data rights in the pre-collection notice where practicable.

citation.anchor: the rights of data subject specified under section 26

rules.scenario: a registration process silently collects personal information
rules.guidance: Make the collection apparent to the patient before collecting the information where practicable.

citation.anchor: the fact that personal data is being collected

rules.scenario: a patient asks the purpose of a registration request
rules.guidance: Explain the collection purpose before collecting the requested information where practicable.

citation.anchor: the purpose for which the personal data is being collected

rules.scenario: a registration notice leaves out recipients and safeguards
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team include the relevant third-party transfer information and safeguards in the notice.

citation.anchor: the third parties whose personal data has been or will be transferred

rules.scenario: a patient cannot identify whom to contact about registration data
rules.guidance: Provide the responsible controller or processor contact information and explain whether another entity may receive the data.

citation.anchor: the contacts of the data controller or data processor

rules.scenario: a patient asks how collected registration information is protected
rules.guidance: Provide the approved description of organizational and technical safeguards rather than inventing security guarantees.

citation.anchor: a description of the technical and organizational security measures

rules.scenario: a patient asks whether a registration field is compulsory
rules.guidance: Explain the applicable basis and whether collection is voluntary or mandatory; refer uncertain requirements to the responsible team.

citation.anchor: whether such collection is voluntary or mandatory

rules.scenario: a patient asks what happens if information is not supplied
rules.guidance: Explain the documented consequences of not supplying the requested information rather than inventing penalties or denying care automatically.

citation.anchor: the consequences if any, where the data subject fails to provide

rules.scenario: a system is being designed to handle patient information
rules.guidance: Include effective data-protection measures in the system design and refer the design to the responsible data team.

citation.anchor: implement the data protection principles in an effective manner

rules.scenario: a workflow adds a new patient-data processing step
rules.guidance: Integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing step rather than adding them only after deployment.

citation.anchor: integrate necessary safeguards for that purpose into the processing

rules.scenario: a team plans to review privacy only after launch
rules.guidance: Review safeguards when choosing how to process data and while the processing operates.

citation.anchor: both at the time of the determination of the means

rules.scenario: a system enables every registration field by default
rules.guidance: Review default collection settings so only data necessary for the specific purpose is processed.

citation.anchor: the amount of personal data collected

rules.scenario: a system enables broad secondary processing by default
rules.guidance: Limit default processing to what is necessary for each specified purpose.

citation.anchor: the extent of its processing

rules.scenario: a system has no default retention setting
rules.guidance: Have the data owner configure purpose-appropriate storage periods within the approved retention process.

citation.anchor: the period of its storage

rules.scenario: a patient-data system grants broad access by default
rules.guidance: Have the access owner limit default accessibility to what is necessary for the specified processing purpose.

citation.anchor: its accessibility

rules.scenario: a system access review begins
rules.guidance: Identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the patient information under the facility's control.

citation.anchor: identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks

rules.scenario: a security review identifies a patient-data risk
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team establish and maintain safeguards proportionate to the identified risk.

citation.anchor: establish and maintain appropriate safeguards

rules.scenario: a team chooses safeguards for patient information
rules.guidance: Consider pseudonymisation and encryption as part of the responsible team's security assessment; do not claim they remove every risk.

citation.anchor: pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data

rules.scenario: a technical incident interrupts record access
rules.guidance: Escalate to the recovery team to restore availability and access in a timely manner under the approved recovery process.

citation.anchor: restore the availability and access to personal data

rules.scenario: a security control has been documented but not checked
rules.guidance: Verify that the safeguards are actually implemented effectively rather than relying only on a written policy.

citation.anchor: verify that the safeguards are effectively implemented

rules.scenario: a new weakness affects a patient-data system
rules.guidance: Refer the weakness for assessment and update safeguards in response to the new risk or deficiency.

citation.anchor: continually updated in response to new risks

rules.scenario: a team selects network security measures
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team consider available technology when selecting appropriate security measures.

citation.anchor: the state of technological development available

rules.scenario: a team compares security implementation options
rules.guidance: Include implementation cost in the security assessment alongside data sensitivity and processing risks; cost alone does not determine suitability.

citation.anchor: the cost of implementing any of the security measures

rules.scenario: a data-transfer workflow is assessed for security
rules.guidance: Assess the specific risks of the processing when choosing organizational and technical measures.

citation.anchor: the special risks that exist in the processing

rules.scenario: a generic security configuration is proposed for health records
rules.guidance: Consider the nature of the patient data rather than assuming a generic configuration is suitable.

citation.anchor: the nature of the data being processed

rules.scenario: a vendor is proposed to process patient information
rules.guidance: Have the controller assess whether the processor provides sufficient organizational safeguards before engagement.

citation.anchor: processor who provides sufficient guarantees

rules.scenario: a vendor asks to start processing without written terms
rules.guidance: Refer the engagement for a written controller-processor contract that limits processing to the controller's instructions and obligations.

citation.anchor: the data controller and the data processor shall enter into a written contract

rules.scenario: a processor proposes using patient data outside instructions
rules.guidance: Stop and escalate the proposed deviation to the controller; the Act changes the processor's role for processing beyond instructions.

citation.anchor: processes personal data other than as instructed

rules.scenario: a contractor handles patient information
rules.guidance: Ensure people acting under the controller's or processor's authority follow the relevant security measures.

citation.anchor: any person employed by or acting under the authority

rules.scenario: a patient-access request asks why records are processed
rules.guidance: Include the processing purposes in the response prepared by the responsible data-access team.

citation.anchor: the purposes of the processing

rules.scenario: a patient-access request asks which data categories are held
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team provide the categories of personal information concerned.

citation.anchor: the categories of personal data concerned

rules.scenario: a patient asks who receives their information
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team identify recipients or recipient categories, including those in other countries or territories.

citation.anchor: the recipients or categories of recipient

rules.scenario: a patient asks how long their information is retained
rules.guidance: Provide the envisaged storage period where possible, or the criteria used to determine it, through the responsible data team.

citation.anchor: the envisaged period for which the personal data may be stored

rules.scenario: a person needs emergency help at the facility
rules.guidance: Alert the qualified emergency-care team promptly and facilitate access to emergency treatment; administrative staff must not diagnose or assign clinical priority.

citation.anchor: Every person has the right to emergency medical treatment

rules.scenario: the first provider lacks capacity to stabilize a patient
rules.guidance: Escalate to the healthcare provider to arrange the necessary referral; administrative staff support coordination and do not decide clinical suitability.

citation.anchor: arranging for referral in cases where the health provider

rules.scenario: staff are uncertain about consent paperwork during an emergency
rules.guidance: Escalate the consent question immediately to the treating healthcare provider; reception must not independently delay emergency care or decide a consent exception.

citation.anchor: the patient is being treated in an emergency situation

rules.scenario: a receptionist is asked to make a clinical decision
rules.guidance: Refer the decision to an appropriately qualified healthcare provider and remain within the administrative role.

citation.anchor: within their scope of practice and ability

rules.scenario: a patient wants to complain about treatment at the facility
rules.guidance: Explain the facility's complaint route and facilitate appropriate investigation rather than dismissing the complaint.

citation.anchor: right to file a complaint about the manner

rules.scenario: staff cannot locate the applicable complaints procedure
rules.guidance: Obtain the published national or county complaints procedure applicable to the facility through its responsible management team.

citation.anchor: establish and publish the procedure for the laying of complaints

rules.scenario: a patient cannot find complaint instructions
rules.guidance: Ensure the complaints procedure is visibly displayed and communicated to service users.

citation.anchor: be displayed by all health facilities

rules.scenario: a complaint reaches reception
rules.guidance: Route the complaint to the facility head or the person designated to handle user complaints.

citation.anchor: primarily handled by the head of the relevant facility

rules.scenario: a complainant asks when a written outcome is due
rules.guidance: Route the complaint for the statutory written update within three months of lodging; do not promise a shorter unapproved deadline.

citation.anchor: within a period of three months from the date

rules.scenario: a suspected harmful unauthorized disclosure is discovered
rules.guidance: Escalate promptly to the controller's incident team to assess notification to the Data Commissioner without delay and within seventy-two hours of awareness when the statutory threshold applies.

citation.anchor: notify the Data Commissioner without delay

rules.scenario: a harmful breach may require informing affected patients
rules.guidance: Have the controller assess written communication to affected patients within a reasonably practical period, including the statutory exceptions.

citation.anchor: communicate to the data subject in writing

rules.scenario: a required breach notification is late
rules.guidance: Escalate the late notification to the responsible controller and include reasons for the delay in the notification.

citation.anchor: the notification shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay

rules.scenario: a processor discovers a patient-data breach
rules.guidance: Escalate for notification to the controller without delay and, where reasonably practicable, within forty-eight hours of awareness.

citation.anchor: within forty-eight hours of becoming aware

rules.scenario: a breach communication is being prepared
rules.guidance: Include a description of the nature of the breach in the communication prepared by the responsible incident team.

citation.anchor: description of the nature of the data breach

rules.scenario: a breach communication omits response measures
rules.guidance: Include the measures already taken or intended to address the breach.

citation.anchor: intends to take or has taken to address the data breach

rules.scenario: a breach communication needs patient-protection information
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team include recommended protective measures appropriate to the security compromise.

citation.anchor: mitigate the adverse effects of the security compromise

rules.scenario: a breach investigation identifies an unauthorized recipient
rules.guidance: Where applicable, include the unauthorized recipient's identity in the communication prepared by the responsible incident team.

citation.anchor: the identity of the unauthorised person

rules.scenario: a breach notice lacks a contact for questions
rules.guidance: Include the data protection officer's details where applicable, or another contact point for further information.

citation.anchor: name and contact details of the data protection officer

rules.scenario: a breach investigation has incomplete information
rules.guidance: Have the responsible team provide information in phases without undue delay when it cannot all be provided at once.

citation.anchor: the information may be provided in phases

rules.scenario: an incident is being documented
rules.guidance: Record the facts relating to the breach in the controller's incident record.

citation.anchor: the facts relating to the breach

rules.scenario: a breach record omits the impact
rules.guidance: Record the effects of the breach as part of the controller's incident documentation.

citation.anchor: its effects

rules.scenario: a resolved incident lacks a corrective-action record
rules.guidance: Record the remedial action taken as part of the controller's breach documentation.

citation.anchor: the remedial action taken

rules.scenario: an unidentified person requests a child's data
rules.guidance: Route the request for appropriate identification of the person exercising the child's rights before disclosing data.

citation.anchor: a person exercising the right is appropriately identified

rules.scenario: a proposal profiles children for promotional messaging
rules.guidance: Escalate and reject the proposed child profiling for direct marketing.

citation.anchor: profiling of a child that is related to direct marketing is prohibited

rules.scenario: a representative's authority to exercise data rights is unclear
rules.guidance: Refer the request for verification; the responsible team may restrict it until evidence of the relationship is provided.

citation.anchor: uncertain as to the existence of a relationship
